title: Apply security principles to site and facility design: concept decisions 1
teachingQuestion: Which site condition and asset consequence determine the facility layer, safety behavior, and recovery plan?
focalInsight: Facility design combines zones, environment, people, response, safety, and continued operation.
caption: Read across a row to connect meaning, decision and consequence. Use the retrieval answer to check your explanation after reading the linked scenario.

nodes.label: Facility Security
nodes.definition: Coordinated physical protection of people, sites, assets, operations, and recovery.
nodes.detail: Coordinated physical protection of people, sites, assets, operations, and recovery.
nodes.decision: Start with asset criticality, safety, site threats, utilities, occupancy, and continuity needs.
nodes.failureExample: A facility plan focuses on locks but ignores flood exposure and emergency egress.
nodes.retrievalAnswer: Facility security is a site-and-operation design problem.

nodes.label: Physical Security
nodes.definition: Controls that deter, delay, detect, assess, respond to, and recover from physical threats.
nodes.detail: Controls that deter, delay, detect, assess, respond to, and recover from physical threats.
nodes.decision: Layer controls from public space to critical assets based on consequence.
nodes.failureExample: A locked room has unmanaged visitor access and no alarm response.
nodes.retrievalAnswer: A barrier is effective only with accountable operation and response.

nodes.label: Site Selection
nodes.definition: Choice of location based on threat, access, utilities, neighbors, emergency services, and recovery needs.
nodes.detail: Choice of location based on threat, access, utilities, neighbors, emergency services, and recovery needs.
nodes.decision: Evaluate natural, crime, infrastructure, legal, and operational factors before commitment.
nodes.failureExample: A data center is placed in a flood-prone area without alternate capability.
nodes.retrievalAnswer: Location can create risk no internal control fully offsets.

nodes.label: Defense In Depth
nodes.definition: Layered physical zones and safeguards that do not rely on one barrier.
nodes.detail: Layered physical zones and safeguards that do not rely on one barrier.
nodes.decision: Separate public, reception, work, restricted, and equipment areas with complementary controls.
nodes.failureExample: A single badge reader is the only protection for a critical room.

nodes.label: Crime Prevention Through Environmental Design
nodes.definition: Use of visibility, lighting, territorial cues, and controlled circulation to reduce opportunity.
nodes.detail: Use of visibility, lighting, territorial cues, and controlled circulation to reduce opportunity.
nodes.decision: Apply when layout can improve observation and legitimate use without defeating safety or accessibility.
nodes.failureExample: A hidden service entrance has poor lighting and no clear boundary.
nodes.retrievalAnswer: Good environmental design can deter and expose unwanted activity.

nodes.label: Safety
nodes.definition: Protection of people and safe operation during normal, emergency, and degraded conditions.
nodes.detail: Protection of people and safe operation during normal, emergency, and degraded conditions.
nodes.decision: Ensure security barriers, alarms, locks, and shutdown behavior preserve life safety and egress.
nodes.failureExample: A lockdown prevents occupants from using an emergency exit.
nodes.retrievalAnswer: Safety constraints govern physical security design.

nodes.label: Perimeter
nodes.definition: Outer boundary controlling approach to a site or protected zone.
nodes.detail: Outer boundary controlling approach to a site or protected zone.
nodes.decision: Use barriers, lighting, monitoring, signage, and response matched to threat and property.
nodes.failureExample: A loading dock provides unmonitored direct entry to a restricted area.
nodes.retrievalAnswer: A perimeter needs controlled crossings and observation.

nodes.label: Restricted Area
nodes.definition: Zone requiring authorization and proportional controls because of asset or process consequence.
nodes.detail: Zone requiring authorization and proportional controls because of asset or process consequence.
nodes.decision: Define purpose, eligible roles, escort rules, access evidence, and emergency behavior.
nodes.failureExample: A contractor uses a shared badge to enter an equipment room.
nodes.retrievalAnswer: Restricted means access is authorized, attributable, and reviewable.

nodes.label: Visitor Management
nodes.definition: Process for identifying, authorizing, escorting, logging, and removing visitor access.
nodes.detail: Process for identifying, authorizing, escorting, logging, and removing visitor access.
nodes.decision: Use when nonemployees need temporary site or restricted-zone access.
nodes.failureExample: A visitor badge remains active after a meeting and permits return access.
nodes.retrievalAnswer: Visitor access needs time-bounded authorization and accountability.
